payload.task_text:
You are a team lead who wants to set up a structured learning program using the most popular technology videos from the Fireship channel. Your task is to curate the top videos and schedule dedicated team viewing sessions in the shared calendar.

Start by querying the video database to find the top 10 most-viewed videos published by the Fireship channel. Rank them from 1 (highest view count) to 10 (lowest).

Create a spreadsheet file called Top_Videos_Watchlist.xlsx in your workspace. This file must contain two sheets.

The first sheet must be named Watchlist. It should have one row per video with the following columns in this exact order: Rank (1 through 10), Video_ID, Title, Duration_Min (the video duration converted to minutes, rounded to 1 decimal place), View_Count, Like_Count, and Like_Rate (calculated as like_count divided by view_count multiplied by 100, rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort rows by View_Count in descending order so Rank 1 is the most-viewed video.

The second sheet must be named Summary. It should have exactly two columns named Label and Value, with the following rows in order: Total_Selected (which should be 10), Combined_Views (the sum of all 10 videos' view counts), Avg_Duration_Min (average duration in minutes rounded to 1 decimal), and Avg_Like_Rate (average like rate across all 10 videos rounded to 2 decimal places).

After creating the spreadsheet, schedule one learning session in the shared calendar for each of the 10 videos. Each event title should be "Team Learning: " followed by the video title truncated to 40 characters if it is longer than 40 characters. Schedule the sessions on consecutive Tuesdays starting April 7, 2026. The first session goes on April 7, the second on April 14, the third on April 21, continuing forward for all 10 sessions. Each session runs from 10:00 AM to 11:00 AM.

Finally, send an email to team@company.com with subject "Learning Sessions Scheduled" and a message body listing all 10 sessions with their scheduled dates and video titles.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Use one stateful Fireship channel-list session: call `channels_listVideos` once at the maximum page size, keep the returned list identifier, and continue only that identifier with `channels_navigateList` until the source is exhausted. Do not restart enumeration. Rank the complete observed catalog by numeric view count, retain exactly the top ten, and compute all Watchlist and Summary values from that table. Create `Top_Videos_Watchlist.xlsx` with one bulk write per sheet and one read-back. From the same ranked table, map ranks 1–10 to the ten Tuesdays from 2026-04-07 through 2026-06-09, and search/create/read back the ten independent 10:00–11:00 events as native-parallel batches, using the task's 40-character title rule and the runtime calendar default because no timezone is specified. Finally send exactly one email to `team@company.com` with subject `Learning Sessions Scheduled` and all ten dates and full titles in chronological order.

TASK: Build an Excel workbook from a prepared, verified JSON data file for a team learning program (top 10 most-viewed Fireship YouTube videos).

CONTEXT: The file /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-yt-top-videos-excel-gcal/workspace/data.json (UTF-8) has already been prepared. It contains:
- "watchlist": array of 10 objects (already sorted by view count descending, rank 1..10) with fields: rank, video_id, title, duration_sec, duration_min, view_count, like_count, like_rate (ignore any underscore-prefixed fields such as _dur_halfup)
- "summary": object with Total_Selected, Combined_Views, Avg_Duration_Min, Avg_Like_Rate
- "events" and "email" keys also exist in the file — IGNORE them entirely (another agent handles those).

OUTPUT FILE (exact path): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-yt-top-videos-excel-gcal/workspace/Top_Videos_Watchlist.xlsx

The workbook must contain EXACTLY two worksheets, in this order:

Sheet 1 — named exactly "Watchlist":
- Row 1 headers, exact names, exact order: Rank, Video_ID, Title, Duration_Min, View_Count, Like_Count, Like_Rate
- Rows 2–11: one row per video in rank order (Rank 1 first), mapping JSON fields: rank→Rank, video_id→Video_ID, title→Title, duration_min→Duration_Min, view_count→View_Count, like_count→Like_Count, like_rate→Like_Rate

Sheet 2 — named exactly "Summary":
- Row 1 headers: Label, Value
- Rows 2–5 in this exact order: Total_Selected, Combined_Views, Avg_Duration_Min, Avg_Like_Rate — each with its value from the JSON "summary" object.

CRITICAL DATA RULES:
- Rank, View_Count, Like_Count, Total_Selected, Combined_Views must be written as integers; Duration_Min, Like_Rate, Avg_Duration_Min, Avg_Like_Rate as floats — exactly the values from the JSON. Do NOT re-round, recompute, or alter them in any way. No formulas — literal values only.
- Video_ID and Title are text and must be copied EXACTLY character-for-character from the JSON. Some titles contain Unicode characters — a curly apostrophe ’ (U+2019), an ellipsis … (U+2026), and straight double quotes " — preserve them exactly; do not normalize, trim, or replace anything.
- No extra sheets, no extra columns, no extra rows, no merged cells, nothing beyond what is specified above.

IMPLEMENTATION: openpyxl 3.1.5 is available in python_execute. Preferred approach: use python_execute with a short script that json.loads data.json and builds the workbook programmatically (so no value is ever retyped by hand). Bold header rows and number formats are optional cosmetics only (e.g. "0.0" for Duration_Min/Avg_Duration_Min, "0.00" for Like_Rate/Avg_Like_Rate) and must not change the stored values.

VERIFY BEFORE REPORTING: reload the saved workbook with openpyxl and programmatically compare EVERY cell of both sheets against data.json — sheet names and their order, header names and order, every value, row order, and numeric types.

REPORT BACK: the file path, the worksheet names in order, and the verification result (exact match yes/no, with details of any discrepancy found and fixed).
Build Top_Videos_Watchlist.xlsx

TASK: Schedule 10 team learning sessions in Google Calendar and send one notification email. This is a team learning program built on the top 10 most-viewed Fireship YouTube videos.

INPUT: Read /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-yt-top-videos-excel-gcal/workspace/data.json (UTF-8). Relevant keys:
- "events": array of 10 objects with fields: rank, date (YYYY-MM-DD), start (e.g. "2026-04-07T10:00:00"), end (e.g. "2026-04-07T11:00:00"), title (the exact calendar event summary), description (a YouTube URL), video_title
- "email": object with to, subject, body

STEP 1 — Create exactly 10 calendar events, one per object in "events" (the dates are consecutive Tuesdays: 2026-04-07, 2026-04-14, 2026-04-21, 2026-04-28, 2026-05-05, 2026-05-12, 2026-05-19, 2026-05-26, 2026-06-02, 2026-06-09):
- summary (title) = the "title" field EXACTLY, character-for-character. WARNING: some titles contain Unicode characters (curly apostrophe ’ U+2019, ellipsis … U+2026, straight double quotes ") and one title legitimately ends with a trailing space — copy them exactly as they appear in the JSON; do not normalize, trim, or "fix" anything.
- start.dateTime = the "start" value exactly as given (floating local time, NO UTC offset); end.dateTime = the "end" value exactly. Do NOT pass a timeZone parameter and do not append offsets — the events must sit at 10:00 AM–11:00 AM local time on their date.
- description = the "description" field (YouTube URL)
- No attendees, no recurrence — single one-hour events.

STEP 2 — Verify: list calendar events in the range 2026-04-01 to 2026-06-30 and confirm there are exactly 10 events with the correct dates, 10:00–11:00 times, and exact titles. If any event is wrong, fix it (update it, or delete and recreate) before proceeding.

STEP 3 — Send the email (only after the events are created and verified):
- to: team@company.com
- subject: Learning Sessions Scheduled
- body: the exact "body" string from data.json, character-for-character (preserve all Unicode characters — ’ … " — and all line breaks). Plain-text body only — no HTML version, no attachments, no CC/BCC.

REPORT BACK: for each of the 10 events — its date and exact title (plus event ID if the tool returns one); the step-2 verification outcome (any mismatch found and fixed); and confirmation that the email was sent (to + subject).
